summary:
OFOQ – An Immersive Journey Through Apollo 15

OFOQ is an educational, interactive virtual reality experience inspired by NASA’s Apollo 15 mission. Using NASA mission data, historical records, and technical documentation, we developed an immersive lunar environment where players take on the role of space archaeologists, investigating equipment left behind on the Moon and uncovering the stories behind it.

Players explore a reconstructed lunar surface, examine 3D models of historical equipment, and discover clues revealing the origins, purposes, and scientific significance of objects from the Apollo 15 mission. Through interactive exploration and storytelling, OFOQ introduces players to the technology, engineering, and history behind lunar exploration.

Our project addresses the challenge of making NASA’s historical and scientific resources more accessible and engaging, particularly for younger audiences. By transforming real mission records into an interactive investigation, OFOQ encourages curiosity, scientific learning, and a deeper appreciation of humanity’s achievements in space exploration.
details:
Project Details – OFOQ: Apollo 15, Abandoned, Not Forgotten

OFOQ is an interactive, browser-based 3D virtual reality experience inspired by NASA’s Apollo 15 mission. It transforms historical mission records into an educational investigation in which players take on the role of space archaeologists, exploring a reconstructed lunar environment and uncovering the origins, purposes, and scientific significance of equipment left behind on the Moon.

The experience follows three main stages: explore, investigate, and understand. Players navigate the lunar environment, examine reconstructed equipment, and discover historical clues that explain the technology and science behind the mission. The investigation combines interactive storytelling with real historical information, allowing users to experience space history rather than simply read about it.

The project was developed using JavaScript and A-Frame. Its modular architecture separates the main functions into four systems: world.js, which builds the lunar environment, terrain, rovers, and lighting; data.js, which stores mission facts, stories, and historical sources; mission.js, which tracks discoveries and completed activities; and app.js, which connects the systems and manages controls, interactions, menus, and saved progress.

To support historical accuracy, we consulted NASA’s Image and Video Library, the Apollo 15 Mission Report, and technical documentation about the Lunar Roving Vehicle and scientific instruments. We also considered gameplay simplicity, educational value, technical feasibility, user engagement, and the accuracy of the reconstructed equipment and historical clues.

OFOQ’s creative approach lies in presenting lunar exploration as an investigation rather than a conventional educational lesson. By combining 3D reconstruction, interactive gameplay, and historical storytelling, it makes NASA’s scientific and historical resources more accessible and engaging. Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, strengthen interest in STEM, and give historical lunar equipment a new educational purpose.

We describe OFOQ as a documentary you can enter.
